Looking at this question about the paper "Assembly of a biocompatible triazole-linked gene by one-pot click-DNA ligation" (Zhang et al., Nature Chemistry, 2016), I need to determine the excitation wavelength used for the fluorescently tagged iLOV gene.

The iLOV gene in this study was tagged with a green fluorescent protein (GFP) for detection. GFP has an excitation peak around 488nm, and in fluorescence measurements, 460nm is a standard excitation wavelength commonly used for GFP detection in plate readers and fluorescence assays.

Among the options provided, 460nm is the most appropriate excitation wavelength for a GFP-tagged construct, as it aligns with standard GFP excitation settings used in fluorescence spectroscopy.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
